cf.title: Add explicit warnings about unsafe OAuth trace output for libpq

input.subject: Add explicit warnings about unsafe OAuth trace output for libpq

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated: PGOAUTHDEBUG trace output contains bearer tokens and client secrets, and the output carries no warning. The change is two stderr messages in one file, seen only by users who set the unsafe trace flag, so it costs other users nothing. Confidence is medium because the wording and the exit paths could not be checked without the code.

brief.title: Warn on stderr when PGOAUTHDEBUG trace output may expose secrets
brief.problem: With PGOAUTHDEBUG trace enabled, libpq-oauth prints raw HTTP traffic to stderr, including bearer tokens and client secrets. The documentation already calls this unsafe, but the output itself carries no warning. Users who paste the long output into bug reports or mailing list posts may not notice that it contains secrets.
brief.proposed_design: libpq-oauth prints a warning at the start of the OAuth flow, right after it parses the debug flags, saying trace logging is active and includes secrets. At the end of the flow, on success or failure, it prints a reminder that the trace output above may contain secrets and should not be shared. The author also offers a Postgres 18 version, where the trigger is PGOAUTHDEBUG=UNSAFE.
user_visible_surface: Two new warning messages on stderr that bracket the libcurl verbose trace when PGOAUTHDEBUG trace (master) or PGOAUTHDEBUG=UNSAFE (18) is set.
author_claims: The warnings mark the start and end of the sensitive output, however much output curl produces in between.
The change is useful to backport to 18, which needs a separate patch because 19 changed the debug flags.
brief.thread_state: Daniel Gustafsson supports the idea and proposes to go ahead unless someone objects; nobody else replied. The author has rebased the same patches twice, and the entry is in its third CommitFest.
unclear: The material does not give the exact wording of the two warnings.
The proposal does not say whether the end warning appears when the flow aborts early or the process exits.
The proposal does not say whether the warnings go through the same stderr path as the curl trace, or whether an application can capture or suppress them.
The thread has no decision on backpatching to 18.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The warnings concern bearer tokens and client secrets that PGOAUTHDEBUG trace prints to stderr.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The author offers a separate patch for 18, where the trigger is PGOAUTHDEBUG=UNSAFE; the thread has no backpatch decision.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does the end warning print on every exit path, including an early abort of the flow or a failure before the first HTTP request?
What is the exact wording of the two warnings, and is it the same on 18 and on master?
Do the warnings go to the same stderr stream as the libcurl trace, so that a redirect captures them together with the secrets?
Is the 18 patch meant for backpatching, given that it adds new stderr output in a stable branch?

committability.owner_note: The owner should know the libpq-oauth client flow in oauth-curl.c. According to the brief, Daniel Gustafsson supports the idea in message #4 and proposes to go ahead unless someone objects.
committability.liability: Two stderr messages in one file, kept in step with the debug flag parsing. With a backpatch, the owner also signs for new stderr output on 18 for users of PGOAUTHDEBUG=UNSAFE.
committability.author_follow_up: The author rebased the patches twice, in messages #2 and #3, and moved the entry through three CommitFests.

priority.reason: Only users who enable unsafe OAuth trace debugging see the change, and for them it lowers the risk of sharing secrets. The patch is under 3 KiB in one file, and the brief reports support in message #4.

provisional_note: The wording of the warnings, the end warning on early-abort paths and the stderr path they use could not be checked without the code. The pass at levels 1-2 is provisional on those points.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: OAuth Followup Patches
precedents_retrieved.summary: Follow-up patches to the OAUTHBEARER SASL authentication support in libpq and the server, which uses the OAuth Device Authorization flow through libcurl. The visible work moves the libcurl-based flow into a separate libpq-oauth module loaded by dlopen() and fixes build and packaging problems on several platforms.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The libpq-oauth module split and its build fixes were committed in May 2025, and the author said he would move a remaining libcurl file-descriptor bug on BSD to its own thread.

precedents_retrieved.title: Missing dependency on oauth_validator test
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the `oauth_hook_client` binary as a test dependency in the oauth_validator meson.build file, so the binary is built before the test runs. Without it, `meson test --suite oauth_validator` failed when the build did not enable the OAuth test through `PG_EXTRA_TEST`.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The only message is the author's proposal, and there are no replies.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve OAuth discovery logging [accidental duplicate]
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch stops the server from logging a FATAL OAuth bearer authentication failure when a client sends an empty token to discover the issuer URL. It adds a new SASL exchange status, PG_SASL_EXCHANGE_ABANDONED (first named PG_SASL_EXCHANGE_RESTART), which auth-sasl.c maps to STATUS_EOF.
precedents_retrieved.objection: This commitfest entry was a duplicate of entry 6529, which Jacob Champion created by mistake and then withdrew. The patch itself was not rejected, and he said the other entry was in his commit queue.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
(I didn't read adequately and ended up duplicating the patch in CF;
I've withdrawn that.

precedents_retrieved.title: libpq trace log
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch began as a libpq client-side query log enabled by connection parameters or environment variables (logdir/PGLOGDIR, logsize/PGLOGSIZE). After review it was narrowed to reworking PQtrace() so it prints one line per protocol message with a timestamp, and enabling it without recompiling was deferred.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Earlier, David Steele moved the patch to PG13 because, in agreement with Andres, it was not clear where the patch was going. The last message before the decision is a review by Alvaro Herrera, who agreed with the one-line-per-message direction but asked for changes. He objected to a frontend_entry[MAXPGPATH] array in pg_conn and listed smaller fixes. The thread shows no new patch or author reply after that review before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This seems to make pg_conn much larger than we'd like.

precedents_retrieved.title: User functions for building SCRAM secrets
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Daniel Gustafsson, Michael Paquier, Magnus Hagander
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a SQL function, scram_build_secret_sha256, that builds a SCRAM-SHA-256 secret from a plaintext password, with an optional salt and iteration count. Its purpose is a SQL equivalent of the hashing done for CREATE/ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD, for uses such as password history checks and precomputing secrets for a remote server.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected that the function requires sending the plaintext password to the server, where it can end up in logs, and SCRAM was meant to avoid that. They suggested other directions: more flexible \password and libpq, GUCs for SCRAM parameters, or a predefined role for changing one's own password. They also questioned allowing a user-chosen salt or low iteration counts. The discussion did not reach consensus, and the entry was returned with feedback after about eight months without activity.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Allowing scram_build_secret_sha256('password', 'a', 1); with the password potentially going in cleartext over the wire and into the logs doesn't seem like a great tradeoff for the (IMHO) niche usecases it would satisfy.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_tracing
precedents_retrieved.summary: A contrib-style extension, pg_tracing, generates distributed-tracing spans for planner, executor and nested queries, using trace context passed in SQLCommenter comments or a sampling rate. Spans go into a shared memory buffer, and an external forwarder reads them with pg_tracing_consume_spans() and sends them to a trace collector.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas recommended that the author publish pg_tracing as a separate extension on GitHub, and Nikita Malakhov agreed. Heikki's own message is not shown; only the replies quote it. In March 2024 the author said he was moving pg_tracing to a GitHub repository, and the entry was later withdrawn. The visible messages do not show a technical objection that blocked the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: To give a quick update: following Heikki's suggestion, I'm currently working on getting pg_tracing as a separate extension on github.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "libpqwalreceiver: Convert to libpq-be-fe-helpers.h"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "libpqwalreceiver: Convert to libpq-be-fe-helpers.h"
Reverted commit(s): libpqwalreceiver: Convert to libpq-be-fe-helpers.h
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 728f86fec65537eade8d9e751961782ddb527934.

The signal handling was a few bricks shy of a load in that commit,
which made the walreceiver non-responsive to SIGTERM while it was
waiting for the connection to be established. That prevented a standby
from being promoted.

Since it was non-essential refactoring, let's revert it to make v16
work the same as earlier releases. I reverted it in 'master' too, to
keep the branches in sync. The refactoring was a good idea as such,
but it needs a bit more work. Once we have developed a complete patch
with this issue fixed, let's re-apply that to 'master'.

precedents_retrieved.title: Report tranche ID and LWLock pointer in LWLock static tracepoints
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds the LWLock pointer and the numeric tranche ID to each LWLock static tracepoint, so traces can tell individual locks apart and compare them across processes. It also fixes misplaced tracepoints, adds a single tracepoint for all acquires and releases plus start markers for timing, and adds comments on LWLock tranches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Two parts were committed by Peter Eisentraut: the removal of the wrong lwlock__acquire tracepoint in LWLockWaitForVar, and the move of TRACE_POSTGRESQL_LWLOCK_RELEASE. In his last review he reported that patch 0002 did not build on macOS because uint64 was used in the probe definitions, and that the probe changes had no documentation. He also asked for a different argument order and whether both tranche name and tranche ID are needed. The visible messages show no new version after that review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
First, a problem:  0002 doesn't build on macOS, because uint64 has been
used in the probe definitions.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use role name "system_user" instead of "user" for unsafe_tests
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andrew Dunstan, Tom Lane, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch renames the role "user" to "system_user" in the rolenames test of the unsafe_tests suite. The test fails when the OS user running it is named "user", and "system_user" is also a keyword but seemed a less likely OS user name.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrew Dunstan said the tests cannot protect against every possible OS user name, and Tom Lane said "system_user" might be as likely an OS user name as "user", or more likely. The author then offered to remove the tests for "user", but Michael Paquier wanted to keep them because the handling of SQL keywords as role names is easy to break. The author withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It only reduces the likelihood if you assume that "system_user"
is less likely than "user" as a choice of OS user name to run
the tests under.  That seems like a debatable assumption;
perhaps it's actually *more* likely.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return historic snapshot during LR
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return historic snapshot during LR
Reverted commit(s): Don't allow GetTransactionSnapshot() in logical decoding
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 1585ff7387 changed GetTransactionSnapshot() to throw an error
if it's called during logical decoding, instead of returning the
historic snapshot. I made that change for extra protection, because a
historic snapshot can only be used to access catalog tables while
GetTransactionSnapshot() is usually called when you're executing
arbitrary queries. You might get very subtle visibility problems if
you tried to use the historic snapshot for arbitrary queries.

There's no built-in code in PostgreSQL that calls
GetTransactionSnapshot() during logical decoding, but it turns out
that the pglogical extension does just that, to evaluate row filter
expressions. You would get weird results if the row filter runs
arbitrary queries, but it is sane as long as you don't access any
non-catalog tables. Even though there are no checks to enforce that in
pglogical, a typical row filter expression does not access any tables
and works fine. Accessing tables marked with the user_catalog_table =
true option is also OK.

To fix pglogical with row filters, and any other extensions that might
do similar things, revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return a
historic snapshot during logical decoding.

To try to still catch the unsafe usage of historic snapshots, add
checks in heap_beginscan() and index_beginscan() to complain if you
try to use a historic snapshot to scan a non-catalog table. We're very
close to the version 18 release however, so add those new checks only
in master.

roaster_notes.note: The precedent search found no earlier proposal with the same or a similar idea, so no prior rejection reason applies. Message #1 points to an earlier thread on splitting the debug flags; according to message #1, the warning idea was moved out of that thread into this one, so it was not rejected there.

The proposal adds two stderr messages only when a user has set the PGOAUTHDEBUG unsafe trace mode, so it introduces no new syntax, GUC, psql convention, dump content or protocol change. Adding text to opt-in debug output on 18 is unlikely to break a working setup, and the exact wording cannot be checked without the code.

The patch adds two stderr messages in libpq-oauth's client-side flow in oauth-curl.c. It does not touch on-disk format, WAL, replication, catalogs, the wire protocol or a public libpq struct, so this angle finds nothing to object to. The ABI impact of the 18 backport could not be checked without the code, but the commit message describes only output changes.

The patch adds two stderr warnings around trace output that the user already opted into with the UNSAFE prefix, and it changes no privilege, default or exposure. It reduces the chance that secrets get shared, and I found no failure scenario that would justify an objection from the security angle.

No maintenance or fit objection holds up. The change is two stderr messages in one file, src/interfaces/libpq-oauth/oauth-curl.c, and they print only when an explicit UNSAFE debug flag is set. That means no hot-path cost for anyone else, no new API, GUC or catalog state, and nothing later features must keep in sync. Daniel Gustafsson, who knows the area, supports it in message #4. Backpatching to 18 changes stderr output only for users who opted into unsafe tracing. Not checked without the code: whether the end warning prints on early abort.

From the existing-feature angle there is no alternative to name. The documentation already warns about PGOAUTHDEBUG trace output, and the patch puts that warning into the output itself, where users who skip the docs will see it. No extension or other core mechanism does this, so the patch adds no second way to do an existing job.

Demand is no fit for this patch. It adds two stderr lines in one file, and only users who opt in to an UNSAFE debug flag see them, so the cost to other users is close to zero. A committer who knows the area supports it in message #4, and the idea came from an earlier review thread mentioned in message #1.
